BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                                          )
EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR                                                 ) Docket No. 25-00082-UT
REVISION OF ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES                                        )
PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317                                            )

   ORDER ON JOINT MOTION FOR CLARIFICATION AND RECONSIDERATION

        THIS MATTER comes before hearing examiners Keven Gedko and Nicholas Rossi upon

the Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration of Order Establishing Revised Procedural

Schedule and Order Extending Suspension Period for Advice Notice No. 317 (“Motion for

Clarification”), El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE” or “Company”) Response in Opposition to

Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration (“EPE’s Response”), and the Joint Reply to

EPE’s Response (“Joint Reply”). Being duly informed, the Hearing Examiners FIND and

CONCLUDE:

        I.       BACKGROUND1

        1.       On March 27, 2026, EPE filed its Application Seeking Revision of its New Mexico

Retail Electric Rates Pursuant to Advice Notice No. 317 (“Application”). EPE defined the

Application to include not only the underlying pleading, but the entire rate-filing package,

including testimony, exhibits, Rule 530 schedules, workpapers, proposed tariffs, Advice Notice

No. 317, and other supporting documents incorporated into the Application by reference.

        2.       On April 15, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement

Exhibits.

        3.       On April 24, 2026, the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) issued its Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317, which deemed EPE’s


1 This order summarizes relevant background. The full electronic record of this proceeding is available at

https://e360.prc.nm.gov/portal/public/.
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



Application complete as of April 15, 2026, and suspended the proposed rates for an initial period

of nine months, commencing on May 15, 2026.2

        4.       On April 27, 2026, Hearing Examiners Jocelyn Barrett and Elizabeth C. Hurst

issued the Procedural Order, which established a procedural schedule and requirements for this

proceeding, and provided the approved form of Public Notice and the requirements for the

distribution of the Public Notice.

        5.       On June 5, 2026, EPE filed the Declaration of Michelle A. Pedroza in Support of

EPE’s Proof of Notice to Customers, which affirmed the Public Notice was published in a

newspaper of general circulation in each county in New Mexico where EPE provides service on

May 4, 2026, the Public Notice was mailed to EPE’s New Mexico customers by bill stuffer

between May 6, 2026 and June 5, 2026, or was e-mailed to customers who receive their bills

electronically on May 11, 2026, the Public Notice and the complete Application were posted on

EPE’s website on May 1, 2026, and EPE ran social media ads targeting New Mexico customer zip

codes between May 11, 2026 and May 15, 2026, and between June 1, 2026 and June 4, 2026.3

        6.       On June 30, 2026, CLC filed CLC’s Verified Motion to Dismiss EPE’s Application

for Revision of Retail Electric Rates (“CLC’s Motion to Dismiss”).

        7.       On July 2, 2026, CLC filed CLC’s Motion for an Order Compelling EPE to Provide

Responses to Discovery Requests and Tolling the Procedural Order’s Deadlines for Intervenor and

Staff Direct Testimony and Rebuttal Testimony (“CLC’s Motion to Compel”). EPE and Doña Ana

County (“DAC”) each filed a response on July 10, 2026, and CLC filed CLC’s Unopposed Motion


2 Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317 (April 23, 2026) ¶¶ 19, 21.

3 Declaration of Michelle A. Pedroza in Support of El Paso Electric Company’s Proof of Notice to Customers

(June 5, 2025) ¶¶ 6-9.

                                                     2
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



for Leave to Reply to EPE’s Response in Opposition to CLC’s Motion to Compel on July 14, 2026.

         8.       On July 7, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Second Notice of Errata and Filing of

Replacement Exhibits.

         9.       On July 10, 2026, CLC, Doña Ana County (“DAC”), the New Mexico Department

of Justice (“NMDOJ”), and pro se intervenors Dwight Eggers, Stephen Fischmann, and Philip B.

Simpson filed the Expedited Joint Objection and Motion for an Order Rejecting EPE’s Second

Notice of Errata and Staying the Procedural Schedule Pending the Company’s Compliance with

Rule 1.2.2.10(G) NMAC (“Expedited Joint Objection”).

         10.      On July 17, 2026, Hearing Examiner Barrett issued the Sua Sponte Order Vacating

Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and Requiring the Filing of an Amended

Application (“Sua Sponte Order”). On August 4, 2026, Hearing Examiners Barrett and Nicholas

Rossi4 issued the Order Clarifying Sua Sponte Order. The Sua Sponte Order vacated the hearing

and procedural schedule previously established, tolled all pending motion and other deadlines, and

required EPE to file, within twenty-one calendar days, a single amended and restated application

and complete supporting filing package (“Amended Application”).5

         11.      The Sua Sponte Order also required Staff to file a Completeness Report, within

seven calendar days after EPE filed its Amended Application, stating whether the Amended

Application and supporting materials were sufficiently complete, coherent, internally consistent,

and technically usable to permit this proceeding to continue.6



4 The Order Appointing Substitute Co-Hearing Examiner (July 20, 2026), appointed Hearing Examiner Rossi

as substitute Co-Hearing Examiner to substitute for and replace Co-Hearing Examiner Hurst.
5 Sua Sponte Order (July 16, 2026) at 1, and Decretal ¶¶ A through E.

6 Id. Decretal ¶ F.



                                                      3
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



         12.      The Sua Sponte Order established that if Staff concluded that the Amended

Application was complete, coherent, internally consistent, and sufficiently usable, and the Hearing

Examiner agreed, then the Hearing Examiner would issue a new procedural order establishing

dates that are consistent with the then-applicable statutory suspension period, unless the

Commission separately extended the period pursuant to Section 62-8-7(C) NMSA 1978.7

         13.      On August 6, 2026, EPE filed its Amended Application, which EPE asserted to be

a complete amended rate filing package, including the Amended Application and the notice to

customers, testimony, exhibits, Rule 530 schedules, work papers, Rule 440 Amended Files,

accompanying rate schedules, and other supporting documents.8

         14.      On August 13, 2026, Staff filed its Completeness Report, in which Staff stated:

“Staff has undertaken a good faith effort to review EPE’s Amended Application, as directed by

the Sua Sponte Order, and finds that it is sufficiently complete to allow this matter to proceed.”9

         15.      On August 19, 2026, Hearing Examiner Keven Gedko was assigned as Co-Hearing

Examiner to substitute for and replace Co-Hearing Examiner Barrett, and to preside over this

matter with Co-Hearing Examiner Rossi.10

         16.      The Hearing Examiners held a scheduling conference on August 25, 2026.

Representatives of EPE, Staff, NMDOJ, CLC, DAC, New Mexico State University, the Coalition

for Clean Affordable Energy, Western Resource Advocates, the US Department of Defense and

all other Federal Executive Agencies, Walmart, Philip B. Simpson, and Stephen Fischmann were


7 Id. Decretal ¶ J.

8 Amended Application (August 6, 2026) at 2.

9 Completeness Report (August 13, 2026) at 7.

10 Order Appointing Substitute Co-Hearing Examiner (August 19, 2026).



                                                    4
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



in attendance. A revised procedural schedule, the need for any additional notice, the status of

CLC’s Motion to Dismiss, the status of CLC’s Motion to Compel, and the status of the Expedited

Joint Objection, were all discussed.

       17.     Based upon the discussion at the scheduling conference, the Hearing Examiners

and the parties came to agreement on a revised schedule for the filing of direct and rebuttal

testimony, and for the public hearing on this matter. The Hearing Examiners also determined that:

               a. EPE, and any other party besides CLC, would have an opportunity to respond
                  to CLC’s Motion to Dismiss on or before September 8, 2026.

               b. The relief requested in the Expedited Joint Objection had been granted in this
                  docket, and the Expedited Joint Objection was therefore moot.

               c. The CLC Motion to Compel was no longer current, and any issues addressed in
                  CLC’s Motion to Compel that a party determined to require further
                  consideration should be addressed in a new filing that reflected the then current
                  circumstances and status of discovery matters in this docket. Therefore, it was
                  determined that CLC’s Motion to Compel was moot.

               d. Notice of the Amended Application should be conducted via publication on
                  EPE’s website and through a social media campaign conducted by EPE, and
                  that notice should clearly identify that EPE’s Amended Application is an
                  amendment to EPE’s previously noticed Application, and is not the filing of a
                  distinct application for an increase in rates.

       18.     On August 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued the Order Establishing Revised

Procedural Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions (“Revised Procedural Order”), in

which the Hearing Examiners established a revised procedural schedule, ordered EPE to file a

proposed form of website notice for EPE’s Amended Application, and ordered EPE to describe

the manner in which EPE would conduct a social media campaign, including a description of how

the social media campaign would connect customers to the form of notice that would be made

available on EPE’s website. The Hearing Examiners also ordered that on or before September 10,

2026, parties were permitted to file comments on EPE’s proposed form of website notice and

                                                5
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



EPE’s filed plan for its social media campaign. Finally, the Hearing Examiners committed to

confirming and/or defining the final form of website notice, and social media campaign, on or

before September 15, 2026.

       19.     On August 28, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued the Order Extending

Suspension Period for Advice Notice No. 317 (“Suspension Order”), which suspended the

proposed rates filed by EPE in Advice Notice No. 317 for an additional two months, until April

15, 2027.

       20.     On September 3, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Notice of Compliance Filing of Proposed

Form of Website Notice.

       21.     On September 8, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Response in Opposition to CLC’s Motion

to Dismiss.

       22.     Also on September 8, 2026, CLC, DAC, Stephen Fischmann and Philip B. Simpson

(“Joint Movants”) filed the Motion for Clarification.

       23.     On September 10, 2026, CLC filed CLC’s Comments on EPE’s Proposed Second

Notice to EPE Customers and Social Media Campaign.

       24.     On September 15, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued the Order on EPE’s

Proposed Second Notice and Social Media Campaign, and required EPE to file additional

information to supplement the information EPE had included in EPE’s Notice of Compliance

Filing of Proposed Form of Website Notice.

       25.     On September 18, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Response to Order on EPE’s Proposed

Second Notice and Social Media Campaign.

       26.     On September 24, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued the Order Defining Second



                                                6
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



Notice and Social Media Campaign, including the approved form of the Second Notice to

Customers.

        27.        On September 21, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Response.

        28.        On September 28, 2026, CLC, DAC, Stephen Fischmann, Philip B. Simpson, and

Dwight Eggers filed the Joint Motion For an Order Rejecting EPE’s Late-Filed Response in

Opposition to the Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration or, in the Alternative, for

Leave to Reply to that Response.

        29.        On September 29, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued the Order Denying Joint

Motion to Reject EPE’s Response and Granting Request to File Reply, which admitted the Joint

Reply into this docket.

        II.        DISCUSSION

        30.        In its Conclusion, the Motion for Clarification asks the Commission to do four

things, which are clearly numbered 1 through 4.11 The Hearing Examiners will consider each of

those requests in turn, as well as one additional request that was included in the Motion for

Clarification.12

                   A. The Motion for Clarification asks the Commission to “clarify
                      whether the Suspension Order is meant to be a recommended
                      decision or certified question to the Commission and, if it is meant
                      to be a final determination on the suspension period, to reconsider
                      that ruling in light of the law and the state of the record in this case,
                      including issues raised in this Joint Motion.”13

        31.        The Suspension Order was issued as a final determination on the suspension period.


11 Motion for Clarification (Sept. 8, 2026) at 26.

12 Other items were included in Section II of the Motion for Clarification, however, as they were excluded

from the Conclusion’s prayer for relief, we decline to address all items.
13 Motion for Clarification at 26.



                                                        7
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



        32.      The Commission appointed the Hearing Examiners to preside over this matter, take

all action necessary and convenient within the limits of the Hearing Examiners’ authority, conduct

any necessary hearings, and take any other action in this case that is consistent with law, including

issuing a recommended decision.” 14 Rule 1.2.2.29(C)(9) NMAC establishes that hearing

examiners have the duty to take appropriate action to avoid delay in the disposition of proceedings,

shall possess all powers necessary to that end, and those powers include taking such action as may

be necessary and appropriate to the discharge of their duties, consistent with the statutory authority

or other authorities under which the Commission functions and with the rules and policies of the

Commission. The Hearing Examiners issued the Suspension Order in accordance with their

appointment by the Commission.

                 B. The Motion for Clarification asks the Commission to “clarify
                    whether the Revised Procedural Order is intended to be a definitive
                    and final ruling on the completeness of EPE’s Amended
                    Application, in light of the denial to intervenors of the opportunity
                    to address that question.”15

        33.      The Revised Procedural Order states: “Staff, having reviewed EPE’s Amended

Application, has opined that the Amended Application is sufficiently complete to allow this matter

to proceed. The Hearing Examiners agree.” This statement expresses the Hearing Examiners’

determination that the Amended Application is sufficiently complete to allow this matter to

proceed. The completeness determination that initiated the statutory period for this proceeding was

made by the Commission on April 24, 2026, when the Commission determined that the



14 Order Appointing Co-Hearing Examiners and Amending Case Caption (April 2, 2026) at 3; See also Order

Appointing Substitute Co-Hearing Examiner (July 20, 2026), and Order Appointing Substitute Co-Hearing
Examiner (August 19, 2026).
15 Motion for Clarification at 26.



                                                   8
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



Application was complete on April 15, 2026.16

        34.      Further, the Joint Movants’ insinuation that the intervenors have been denied the

opportunity to address the completeness of EPE’s Amended Application is incorrect. The Sua

Sponte Order directed Staff to conduct an expedited threshold review of the Amended Application

and to file a report addressing whether the filing was “sufficiently complete, coherent, internally

consistent, and technically usable to permit the proceeding to continue.” Nothing in that Order

prohibited any other party from raising concerns regarding the completeness of the Amended

Application or otherwise responding to Staff’s assessment. Nor did the Order purport to foreclose

further consideration of issues bearing on the adequacy of EPE’s filing though testimony, cross

examination, other motions practice, or any other manner.

                 C. The Motion for Clarification asks the Commission to “clarify
                    whether the Revised Procedural Order and the Suspension Order
                    are intended to reflect a determination that EPE need not submit a
                    new or amended advice notice that corresponds to the rates and the
                    total New Mexico revenue requirement that its Amended
                    Application supports through testimony, exhibits, schedules, and
                    workpapers, as well as to address the implications of EPE’s choice
                    not to amend its Advice Notice No. 317 upon the scope of the
                    litigation of this proceeding.”17

        35.      EPE does not need to submit a new or amended advice notice.

        36.      EPE filed Advice Notice No. 317 on March 17, 2026. NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-

7(B) (2011) and Rule 17.1.2.10(B)(1) NMAC establish that no public utility shall make any change

in any rate that has been duly established except after thirty days’ notice to the Commission.

Advice Notice No. 317 provided such notice to the Commission, and per Rule 17.1.2.10(B)(1)



16 Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317 ¶ 19.

17 Motion for Clarification at 26.



                                                  9
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



initiated this proceeding involving new rates.18

         37.     Advice Notice No. 317 presented the rates that were communicated in the Public

Notice that was published in a newspaper of general circulation in each county in New Mexico

where EPE provides service on May 4, 2026, was mailed to EPE’s New Mexico customers by bill

stuffer between May 6, 2026 and June 5, 2026 or by e-mail to customers who receive their bills

electronically on May 11, 2026, was posted on EPE’s website on May 1, 2026, and was linked to

social media ads targeting New Mexico customer zip codes between May 11, 2026 and May 15,

2026, and between June 1, 2026 and June 4, 2026.19

         38.     In the Amended Application, EPE Witness George Novela testifies that “EPE

accepts that the Commission cannot order rates higher than what were publicly noticed in Advice

Notice No. 317.”20

         39.     In its Completeness Report, Staff recognizes that “while the correction to the

revenue requirement and rate calculations are evident throughout the Amended Application and

the new tariffs, the same is not true for the suspended advice notice.”21 Staff then recognizes the

testimony of Mr. Novela,22 and states: “Staff understands this to mean that EPE is not seeking to

recover the increase to the revenue requirement caused by the second errata and is instead

requesting approval of the noticed rates and revenue requirement included in Advice Notice No.


18
  Rule 17.1.2.10(B)(1): “Proceedings involving new rates shall be initiated by advice notice notifying the
commission of the utility's intent to implement new rates by a certain date which may not be less than 30 days
after the filing of such notice.”
19 Declaration of Michelle A. Pedroza in Support of El Paso Electric Company’s Proof of Notice to Customers

(June 5, 2025) ¶¶ 6-9.
20 Amended Direct Testimony of George Novela (“Novela Amended Direct”)
                                                                              (Aug. 6, 2026) at 12:15-21.
21 Staff’s Completeness Report (August 13, 2026) ¶ 11.

22 Id.



                                                      10
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



317.”23

          40.    Rule 17.1.210 NMAC does not require a new advice notice be filed due to

incomplete filings, corrections to filings, or any other reason. And the rates communicated in an

advice notice, and in a public notice of those rates, are not required to be the rates that ultimately

go into effect.24

          41.    Further, the Hearing Examiners’ Order Defining Second Notice and Social Media

Campaign defined a Second Public Notice and the required distribution of that Second Public

Notice on EPE’s website and through a social media campaign. The distribution of the Second

Public Notice provides a reasonable and clear notice of the filing of EPE’s Amended Application,

and how the rates and tariffs in the Amended Application relate to the rates and tariffs filed in

EPE’s Application.

          42.    In sum, EPE’s proposed change in rates was adequately noticed to the Commission

by EPE’s filing of Advice Notice No. 317, and there is no requirement that a new or revised advice

notice be filed in this proceeding. Further, the public has been sufficiently informed of EPE’s

initially proposed rate changes, the changes to that proposal provided in the Amended Application,

and the fact that EPE accepts that the Commission cannot order rates higher than what were

publicly noticed in Advice Notice No. 317. EPE does not need to submit a new or amended advice

notice in this proceeding.



23 Id.

24 See NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(D): “If after a hearing the commission finds the proposed rates to be

unjust, unreasonable or in any way in violation of law, the commission shall determine the just and reasonable
rates to be charged or applied by the utility for the service in question.” See also 17.1.2.10 NMAC(C)(2)(e),
establishing that public notice of a change in rates shall contain “a statement that the rate changes stated by
class and, for residential customers, by consumption levels are for informational purposes only and that the
final rate design may vary the rates ultimately charged to each class and for each consumption level.”

                                                      11
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



                 D. The Motion for Clarification asks the Commission to “reject EPE’s
                    (Proposed) Second Notice to Customers for the reasons stated in
                    this Motion, including but not limited to the Company’s failure to
                    provide a detailed description of its planned social media campaign
                    or a copy of the advertisement or advertisements it would utilize in
                    that campaign, and to revise the procedural schedule set in the
                    Revised Procedural Order to allow reasonable notice to EPE’s New
                    Mexico retail customers and potential intervenors with sufficient
                    time for them to participate in this proceeding as intervenors.”25

        43.      EPE’s Proposed Second Notice to Customers has been addressed through CLC’s

Comments on EPE’s Proposed Second Notice to Customers, the Hearing Examiners’ Order on

EPE’s Proposed Second Notice and Social Media Campaign, EPE’s Response to Order on EPE’s

Proposed Second Notice and Social Media Campaign, and the Hearing Examiners’ Order Defining

Second Notice and Social Media Campaign. The Hearing Examiners’ orders effectively granted

the request to reject EPE’s Proposed Second Notice to Customers, after which EPE complied with

the Hearing Examiners’ orders regarding the Second Notice and Social Media Campaign, and the

Hearing Examiners then defined the final form of the Second Notice and Social Media Campaign.

        44.      The current procedural schedule, set in the Revised Procedural Order, has provided

and continues to provide EPE’s New Mexico retail customers and potential intervenors with

sufficient time for them to participate in this proceeding as intervenors. As explained above,

extensive public notice of this proceeding was affirmed by EPE’s filing of the Declaration of

Michelle A. Pedroza in Support of EPE’s Proof of Notice to Customers, on June 5, 2026. Public

notice was provided well over 4 months in advance of the October 16, 2026, intervention deadline.

The website and social media campaign, for the Second Public Notice, provides additional public

notice regarding this ongoing proceeding, and is being conducted from September 28, 2026


25 Motion for Clarification at 26.



                                                 12
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



through October 12, 2026, which provides additional time for any additional potential intervenors

to participate in this proceeding.

                E. Additional Clarification

         45.    The Motion for Clarification includes an additional request:

                    “[T]he Joint Parties seek clarification of the scope of the testimony and cross
                    examination of witnesses during the scheduled public hearing. The Joint Parties
                    do not know whether the expectation is that the proposed amended rates of the
                    Amended Application will be litigated, subject to some sort of a cap based on
                    either the originally filed revenue requirement in accordance with Mr. Novela’s
                    testimony or the originally filed revenue requirement and tariffs in accordance
                    with Staff’s Completeness Report.”26

         46.    EPE’s Amended Application and its supporting testimony, exhibits, schedules,

workpapers, and proposed tariffs constitute the operative affirmative filing to be adjudicated in

this proceeding. This does not prohibit reference to the materials filed in this docket prior to the

filing of the Amended Application, during testimony or cross-examination or for otherwise proper

evidentiary purposes, including impeachment, prior inconsistent statements or positions,

comparison of changes, or other relevant matters. Any such use remains subject to applicable

evidentiary and procedural requirements.

         47.    With respect to the Amended Application being “subject to some sort of cap,” EPE

has stated that it accepts that the Commission cannot order rates higher than what were publicly

noticed in Advice Notice No. 317,27 which Staff understands to mean that EPE is not seeking to

recover the increase to the revenue requirement caused by the second errata and is instead

requesting approval of the noticed rates and revenue requirement included in Advice Notice No.



26 Id. ¶ 61.

27 Novela Amended Direct at 12:19-21.



                                                13
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration   Docket No. 25-00082-UT



317.28

         48.     The Hearing Examiners clarify that there is no Statute or Rule that establishes the

Commission cannot order a revenue requirement or rates that are higher than what were publicly

noticed in Advice Notice No. 317.29 Instead, Advice Notice No. 317 met the requirements for the

filing of an advice notice established under Rules 17.1.2.10 NMAC and 17.1.210 NMAC, and this

proceeding now provides the adversarial forum for litigation regarding what revenue requirement

and rates the Commission will ultimately set at the conclusion of this proceeding. The Commission

will set those rates based upon an adjudication of EPE’s Amended Application and its supporting

testimony, exhibits, schedules, workpapers, and proposed tariffs, which is the operative affirmative

filing to be adjudicated in this proceeding.

         IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

         A.      This Order clarifies:

                 1. The Suspension Order was issued as a final determination on the suspension
                    period.

                 2. The Amended Application is sufficiently complete to allow this matter to
                    proceed.

                 3. EPE does not need to submit a new or amended advice notice.

                 4. EPE’s Proposed Second Notice to Customers has previously been addressed
                    in the Hearing Examiners’ Order Defining Second Notice and Social Media
                    Campaign.


28 Completeness Report at 6.

29 See Section 62-8-7(D), establishing that the Commission may, after hearing, set rates that are designed to

produce annual revenues no greater than those determined by the commission in its order to be just and
reasonable. Just and reasonable rates could include rates that exceed the rates included in a filed advice notice.
See also 17.1.2.10(C)(2)(e) NMAC, establishing that rate changes provided in public notice, which initially
communicate the rates proposed in the advice notice that initiates a proceeding, are for information purposes
only and that the final rate design may vary the rates ultimately charged to each class and for each
consumption level. The final rate design could include rates that exceed the rates included in the public notice.

             5. EPE’s Amended Application and its supporting testimony, exhibits,
                schedules, workpapers, and proposed tariffs constitute the operative
                affirmative filing to be adjudicated in this proceeding. This does not prohibit
                reference to the materials filed in this docket prior to the filing of the
                Amended Application, during testimony or cross-examination or for otherwise
                proper evidentiary purposes, including impeachment, prior inconsistent
